q: How much power and CO2 can waste heat recovery save in a 2 x 100 TPD DRI plant?
title: DRI waste heat power: what 5 MW saves
short: About 23.5 million kWh of grid power a year. TERI's 2025 Bankura profile says a 2 x 100 TPD coal-based DRI plant can run a 5 MW waste heat power plant, costing about Rs 500 million, avoiding roughly 15,900 t CO2 at today's grid factor. Better kiln lining saves another 580 t of coal per kiln.
audience: Coal-based sponge iron plants in Bankura, Durgapur and other West Bengal and Jharkhand clusters

p: Off gas leaves a DRI rotary kiln at 950 to 1,000 C. A waste heat boiler turns it into high pressure steam for a turbine; the power runs the plant and any surplus can go to the grid. The kiln shell itself runs at 180 to 250 C, and radiation from it is about 5% of the heat input.

ul: About 37 secondary steel units: DRI, ferro alloy, induction furnace melt shops and re-rolling mills, making about 3.6 million t a year.
10 DRI plants make 1,396,500 t a year on 1.53 million t of coal, 700,875 toe and 2.87 million t CO2 by TERI's count.
DRI is 48% of the cluster's energy; the whole cluster emits about 5.96 million t CO2.
Plants burn both domestic and imported coal.

p: Rs 500 million for 23.5 million kWh a year is about Rs 21 of investment per kWh saved each year. Divide that by what you pay per kWh to get a rough payback before running costs. At an assumed Rs 7 per kWh it is about three years; use your own tariff and steam data.

sections.h: What it does to your carbon numbers
ul: Kiln coal does not change, so direct emissions stay where they are.
Grid purchases fall, so your Scope 2 figure and the footprint a domestic buyer sees fall with them.
Do not put a grid factor on the waste heat power; its fuel is already counted in the kiln.
Sponge iron counts direct emissions only under CBAM, so waste heat power does not lower the CBAM figure. Coal burnt per tonne of sponge iron does.

sections.h: Two kiln changes in the same profile
ul: Mullite-based low conductivity lining on a 100 TPD kiln: about 580 t of coal a year.
Pellets instead of 5 to 20 mm ore lumps: better yield, fewer fines, less coal per tonne.

example.title: Savings at today's factors (estimate)
lines: Waste heat power: 23.5 million kWh x 0.675 kg = about 15,860 t CO2 a year
TERI's profile gives 16,685 t, using a slightly higher grid factor
Better lining: 580 t Indian coal x 1.76 = 1,021 t CO2; imported coal at 2.44 = 1,415 t
Payback: Rs 500 million / (23.5 million kWh x Rs 7) = about 3 years, before running costs
example.note: Plant figures from TERI's 2025 Bankura energy profile. The Rs 7 per kWh tariff is an assumption for the example. Grid factor from CEA for FY 2025-26.

senseible: The green loan check shows what a lender asks before funding a waste heat plant. Senseible reads coal invoices and power bills into monthly records, so the grid power saved shows against your own baseline.
